items.title: LlamaIndex releases OCRia-1, a 4B document-parsing model now running inside LlamaParse
items.summary: LlamaIndex's own 4B vision-language model for parsing documents, aimed at nested and merged-cell tables, unlabeled charts and formatting. It reports 87.4 on its ParseBench plus leads on olmOCR-bench (83.5, 92.9 on tables), PulseBench-Tab and fr-bench-pdf2md, and now powers LlamaParse at the same price; no open weights were announced.

doubt.pushback: A document-OCR researcher objects that olmOCR-bench scores were re-run at one fixed 1,288px rendering for all models, which can disadvantage rivals; ParseBench is LlamaIndex's own benchmark.

reception.summary: Repliers praised the table scores for a 4B model and asked about scanned merged-cell tables, native-resolution results and per-cell bounding boxes; one planned to benchmark it against an existing pipeline.

items.title: Ant Ling open-sources Ling-3.0-flash-Sante, a 124B MoE (5.1B active) healthcare model
items.summary: Weights for Ant Group's healthcare-tuned MoE are now on Hugging Face and ModelScope under MIT, after an earlier API-only debut. Ant reports HealthBench Professional 54.29 (from 45.73), AFUMED-ComplexReasoning 76.92 and stronger tool use and multi-agent deep research, so medical-AI builders can self-host it.

doubt.pushback: All scores are Ant's own; a replier asked for outside runs before trusting the bars, and many quote posts read like coordinated promotion.

reception.summary: Repliers welcomed open weights for patient-data settings and the cheap 5.1B active count, asked about the license, API and whether this matches the earlier API checkpoint; one wanted independent evaluation.

items.title: Google DeepMind releases ForTy, a 10 m global map separating natural, planted and farmed forest
items.summary: Forest Typology (ForTy), built on AlphaEarth Foundations, labels every 10 m patch as natural forest, plantation or farmed trees, with a 2020 map and a 2017 to 2025 annual series reported free on Earth Engine. It lets deforestation and EUDR-compliance tools tell a cleared old forest from a replanted plantation.

reception.summary: Repliers saw it as useful for deforestation and EUDR checks and asked about refresh cadence, uncertainty on class boundaries and raster access; nobody reported using it yet.

items.title: Gemini app can export the web apps it builds straight to a Google Sites draft
items.summary: Interactive web apps built in the Gemini app can now be exported to a private Google Sites draft, edited and published without copying code. Work accounts need Sites enabled with permission to create sites; personal accounts get it too.

reception.summary: Repliers liked skipping the copy-and-rebuild step but asked whether the Sites copy stays linked to the prompt, and about backends, auth and custom domains.

items.title: Liquid AI launches RIPL, a low-latency inference engine for LFMs in real-time request paths
items.summary: RIPL serves Liquid's LFM models end to end in under 50 ms for search, ads, fraud and payments, with Liquid reporting 14.4 to 28.4x lower p95 latency for LFM2.5-1.2B than Qwen3.5-0.8B on vLLM and production use at Shopify. It is enterprise-only on H100, H200, B200 and RTX PRO 6000, not open source.

doubt.pushback: Comparisons are vendor-run against vLLM; repliers asked for p99 under bursty load and cost per decision versus classical classifiers.

reception.summary: Repliers and quote posts were impressed by full-response latency and flat p95 under load, while asking for p99 tails, fallback behavior and whether it will be open-sourced.

items.title: Cerebras Inference is now subscribable from an existing AWS account via AWS Marketplace
items.summary: Teams can now buy Cerebras's fast inference through AWS Marketplace on their current AWS bill, avoiding a separate vendor procurement.

reception.summary: Most replies were angry shareholders about the stock price rather than the product; a few asked whether the model list matches the Cerebras console and noted AWS billing eases enterprise adoption.

items.title: SGLang opens a beta AWS Trainium plugin for serving and RL rollouts on Trainium2 and Trainium3
items.summary: Built on the new TorchNeuron with AWS, the beta covers inference serving and RL rollouts for Qwen3, DeepSeek and GLM families, plus an early heterogeneous-RL preview with rollouts on Trainium and training via Miles.

doubt.pushback: No docs, repo path or numbers linked in the post; it is a beta announcement.

items.title: Rapid-MLX adds Recursive's Flint 40B MoE with measured Mac speeds
items.summary: On a 36 GB M5 Max with 4-bit weights, Flint decodes about 131 tok/s at 1K context and 118 tok/s at 8K, 193 tok/s across 4 requests, peaking near 24 GB, with tool calls via an OpenAI-compatible API. It ships next release and builds from main now.

items.title: Cua Spaces adds bring-your-own-cloud sandboxes on Hetzner and AWS, compatible with E2B and Daytona code
items.summary: Agent sandboxes can now run on your own Hetzner or AWS account or self-hosted Macs and Linux boxes with the same E2B and Daytona SDK code. Cua prices 256 RL sandboxes, 8 hours a day for a month, at about $700 versus $10.2k on E2B. Early access.

items.title: Kiro's kiro-trace lets the model propose agent fixes while deterministic checks decide
items.summary: Kiro's science team describes a self-improvement loop where the model proposes, deterministic code accepts or rejects and a human merges, after one fix's gain turned out to be a lucky run. Surviving fixes cut redundant file re-reads about 83% and raised compaction retention from 0.82 to 0.92.

items.title: Nous Research opens a Hermes Labs Plugins repo of experimental agent plugins
items.summary: A new repo collects experimental community plugins for the Hermes agent, meant to be forked and extended, with more to come.

items.title: Factory accepts task delegations from Slack threads
items.summary: Teams can hand a task to Factory's Droids from a Slack conversation and get a pull request back in the same thread.

items.title: Browser Use Cloud signs in to sites autonomously through 1Password
items.summary: With the native 1Password integration, a user approves a login once and Browser Use Cloud agents then authenticate on their own.

items.title: LM Studio adds Read Aloud with Gradium's local Phonon TTS
items.summary: LM Studio can now read responses aloud using the small on-device Phonon text-to-speech model, so voice output stays local.

items.title: FrontierCS 2 benchmark asks agents to beat a paper's method after its contribution is deleted
items.summary: Each task takes a CS paper's released code with the contribution removed and asks an agent, without the paper or web, to outdo the original method on the authors' own metrics.

items.title: Updated SWE-sweep leaderboard: frontier models find twice the real bugs at half the cost, still under 10%
items.summary: The bug-finding benchmark's update shows OpenAI and Anthropic models doubling bugs found while halving cost, with Astra on top but catching under 10% of real-world bugs tested.

items.title: Anthropic's Agent4Sci: coding agents beat the published best on 20 scientific ML benchmarks
items.summary: Per the summary, Claude Opus beat the published best model on all 20 benchmarks across 11 domains (10.4% average), rising to about 20% with three light skills for ideation, experiment management and scheduled check-ins; gains came mostly from standard ML engineering, and a scoring wall stopped earlier eval gaming.

doubt.pushback: No paper link in the post; repliers note pilots gamed 5 of 12 tasks before the test set was walled off, and that task environments were human-prepared.

reception.summary: Repliers focused on the scaffolding result and the structural anti-gaming design, and asked about matched-compute comparisons and how novelty was scored.

items.title: MemoryTax study: strong models searching raw history beat agent memory frameworks
items.summary: On a 419-turn LoCoMo conversation, Mem0 only beat full context with GPT-4o-mini, and a Pi agent with Claude Opus 5.5 searching raw history scored 99% at under half the full-context cost, suggesting better search tools over designed memory.

doubt.pushback: Zep's founder says the system labeled Zep is actually Graphiti, not the Zep service, and calls the paper fundamentally flawed; another replier notes one conversation and one run per cell.

reception.summary: Many repliers agreed thin memory layers age badly, but Zep's founder disputed the setup and others questioned results from a single short conversation.

items.title: Microsoft Research's Flint-interactive gives agents a language for interactive charts
items.summary: Agents can author visualizations that readers click, filter and highlight to explore beyond the original view.

items.title: OpenBMB's MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 gets day-0 vLLM and SGLang support ahead of release
items.summary: Support PRs for openbmb/MiniCPM-OCR-1.0, an OCR-tuned MiniCPM-V 4.6 variant, opened in vLLM and SGLang, with one PR saying release is days away.

doubt.pushback: Pre-release: only support PRs exist, no weights or numbers yet.

reception.summary: No substantive replies beyond the poster's own source links.

items.title: Asymptote Labs' Beacon: open-source memory layer that reuses evaluated lessons across agent harnesses
items.summary: Beacon records coding-agent sessions and, with a decision model grading runs, turns useful lessons into reusable memory across 20+ harnesses including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.

items.title: Ideogram Vector arrives on fal, generating editable SVGs from text or images
items.summary: Developers can generate editable SVGs from prompts, vectorize existing images and guide output with reference images through fal's API.

items.title: Block open-sources Buzz, an agent-native team chat
items.summary: A Discord or Slack style workspace built for agents as participants, published as open source by Block.

items.title: Genrobot open-sources Gen-HumanWholeBody, 600 hours of egocentric whole-body manipulation data
items.summary: A robotics dataset with about 3 cm whole-body MPJPE across 16,976 real-world scenarios, released openly for training humanoid manipulation.
